mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL over a three-month period indicates a restrictive monetary policy that is successfully reducing inflationary pressures, which supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) combined with stable housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household balance sheets and sustained consumption demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows AND HOUST is stable for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when PAYEMS grows and HOUST is stable for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals a tight labor market and wage inflation, which increases input costs and reduces corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL growth < 2% over same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE falls below 4% for two months in a low inflation environment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (implied by RSAFS growth) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE stable) signals strong consumer demand with stable labor markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when RSAFS grows and UNRATE is stable for two months in an early-cycle recovery.
